hypotheses.statement: Technology adoption cycles have shortened (decades for print; months for generative AI).
hypotheses.evidence_pointing_toward: Run 8d: learning platforms took decades to institutionalise, lockdown-forced remote teaching took days, a widely used generative AI system reportedly saw rapid global uptake within months; the figure remains unverified.
hypotheses.limits: Adoption of tools is not institutional adoption; the three cases measure different things; most evidence is cross-sectional.
hypotheses.next_test: Build adoption-speed layer from coded milestones with explicit definitions.

hypotheses.statement: Institutional response lags have not shortened in proportion, so the gap between technology and institutional change has widened.
hypotheses.evidence_pointing_toward: Run 8d: universities began issuing generative-AI policies within weeks (faster than for earlier technologies) but many highly ranked universities still lacked policies by mid-2023 and responses were fragmented; historical lags to institutional change were decades (Runs 5b).
hypotheses.limits: First-response speed and durable restructuring are different quantities; no longitudinal outcome evidence for any milestone.
hypotheses.next_test: Separate first-response lag from restructuring lag when coding.

hypotheses.statement: Formal institutional forms persist while control and governance shift.
hypotheses.evidence_pointing_toward: Convergent across Runs 4a, 4b, 4c, 5b, 7a, 8a-8d: degrees, campuses and credentials persist; custody, labour, funding and authority move to platforms, publishers, metrics providers and infrastructures.
hypotheses.limits: Abstract-level evidence; much of the evidence for control shifts is critical or conceptual; no longitudinal macro-level evidence.
hypotheses.next_test: Spot-verify the load-bearing sources; look for counter-cases.

hypotheses.statement: Major technological shifts add new organisational forms next to existing ones instead of replacing them.
hypotheses.evidence_pointing_toward: Run 5b and 7a: academies, journals, research universities and corporate laboratories arose alongside existing institutions; combined-format and open universities extended campus universities; replacement predictions for radio, television and MOOCs did not materialise.
hypotheses.limits: Provider-level discontinuities exist (for-profit correspondence colleges); survivorship bias in histories; Run 7a is smaller run-depth.
hypotheses.next_test: larger run re-run of distance HE when credits allow.

hypotheses.statement: Functions of HEIs have repeatedly been unbundled and rebundled with ecosystem actors (academies, societies, publishers, libraries, platforms); what is distinctive in the digital and AI period, if anything, is to be established, not assumed.
hypotheses.evidence_pointing_toward: Runs 8a-8c describe layering and recombination among universities, academies and societies, publishers, libraries and infrastructures; the strongest pattern is institutional plurality under unequal conditions.
hypotheses.limits: Distinctiveness of the present period is untested; coverage concentrated in Britain and the Global North.
hypotheses.next_test: Code the ACTOR dimension and division of labour per milestone.
